The shared tokens (plugin-root, skill-dir-var, cwd-script, relative-link, cross-skill-path, requires-harness:claude) and ALL their semantics — regexes, fence walk, option skipping, existence, ../ resolution — live only in the canonical file and are derived by the same engine crew uses. This file holds what garden's authoring convention adds on top: the exact `## Runtime` block, the harness-fallback sentences, the name-based cross-ref resolver, the slash-form ban, the bare-script-span extension of cwd-script, and the stricter bare-identifier check. launcher.runtime_block:
## Runtime
Script-backed steps use the `wicked-garden` launcher: `wicked-garden run <plugin-root-relative path, e.g. scripts/…> [args]`. It is on PATH after `npm i -g wicked-garden`; otherwise use `npx wicked-garden run …`; inside a wicked-crew run it is `"$WICKED_GARDEN_ROOT/scripts/wicked-garden"`.
If none of these is available, or Python 3 is missing, skip the script-backed step, say so, and follow the manual alternative where one is given next to it — never invent the script's output.
Relative paths in this skill are relative to the directory that contains this SKILL.md.

fallbacks.fork_worker_sentence: This skill is designed to run as an isolated worker; when your harness cannot fork, run it inline and keep its output separate from the caller's.
fallbacks.dispatch_sentence: Dispatch uses the Skill tool on Claude Code (a fresh forked context). On any other harness, open the named skill's `SKILL.md` from your skills catalog and carry out its instructions inline with the given args, then continue here.
fallbacks.skill_name_exemption_marker_scope: token: the marker must directly follow the wicked-garden-<x> token (an optional closing quote/backtick and spaces may sit between); a marker elsewhere on the line exempts nothing

codemod.note: the codemod (scripts/wg/portability_codemod.py, dev tooling) rewrites MORE than the lint judges — yaml/yml fences too, since a CI template's `run:` lines are shell — rewriting toward the launcher is always safe

tokens.garden_extension: garden also fails on the bare identifier CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT anywhere under skills/ (crew: the `${…}` marker only)
garden also fails on the bare identifier CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR

a bare `scripts/<x>.py <args>` code span, or a shell-fence line that starts with such a path and is not a `\` continuation, with no interpreter at all — an instruction no host can execute — when the path exists at the plugin root and not inside the referencing skill

tokens.rule: a wicked-garden-<x> name (prose, .md files) that no SKILL.md declares; template forms (`{`, or followed by `-` as in wicked-garden-qe-{a, b} / wicked-garden-qe-* / wicked-garden-<x>) are skipped; the inline marker `<!-- not-a-skill -->` placed DIRECTLY AFTER a token (`wicked-garden-x` <!-- not-a-skill -->) declares that token an identifier (an evaluator id, a sibling plugin), not a cross-ref — the design scopes this token to dispatch/cross-refs and the marker keeps that declaration next to the text instead of in a central allowlist (which stays empty)
a skill whose own files use `wicked-garden run|python|path` must carry the exact ## Runtime block in its SKILL.md
a /wicked-garden:<x> slash form in a skill BODY (frontmatter descriptions may keep 'former /wicked-garden:x invocation' trigger phrases) — skills are not slash commands on any CLI
a context: fork SKILL.md must carry the fork_worker_sentence
a file that dispatches with Skill(skill=…) — single-line or the multi-line `Skill(\n  skill=…` form — must carry the dispatch_sentence once
a file that mentions AskUserQuestion (outside frontmatter) must also spell the plain-text fallback
